To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of random velocity heterogeneities in a mantle lid structure on the geometric spreading of seismic Pn phases is frequency dependent and that the frequency dependence of P n geometric spreading is a function of the heterogeneity distribution.

(i) the distance dependence of the amplitude of Pn waves from shallow sources is strongly modified by lateral heterogeneity in the mantle lid, (ii) this modification is frequency dependent, and (iii) the frequency‐dependent modification is strongest for frequencies of ∼1–10 Hz

the frequency dependence of P wave geometric spreading is sensitive to the strength and correlation length of random velocity heterogeneities in a mantle lid and that this effect must be accounted for in the interpretation of P wave attenuation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to the analysis of seismic wavefields, based on the concept of the wavefield spectrum.
the study of the seismic properties of the lithosphere and upper mantle.
the study of the effects of the 2D heterogeneities in a mantle lid on the geometric spreading of Pn ‐waves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Pn wave, which is the first seismic-wave arrival at distances of 200 to 1500 km, is expected to exhibit frequency-dependent geometric spreading for most velocity structures.

the Pn phase is frequency dependent, and this dependence is not only due to the attenuation of the Pn wave, but it is also due to the interference of multiple reflections from the Mohorovičić discontinuity, which can be affected by the heterogeneity of the mantle.

the frequency‐dependent effects of 2D mantle lid heterogeneities on Pn geometric spreading have been quantified for a wide range of frequencies, and that these effects are stronger than those predicted for a 1‐dimensional model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of heterogeneities in a model mantle lid can significantly affect the Pn geometric spread.

the frequency dependence of P wave geometric spreading is controlled by the interference of multiple underside Moho reflections, and the interference pattern is sensitive to the velocity and topography of the mantle lid, as well as to the velocity of the crust and Moho.

, although 2D random velocity heterogeneity in the uppermost mantle lid can have a strong impact on the Pn amplitude‐distance behavior at frequencies of ∼1 Hz, the effects become more subtle at higher frequencies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the frequency dependence of P wave attenuation and scattering can only be reliably separated from the frequency dependence of geometric spreading for Pn if both the frequency dependence of the Pn geometric spread and the heterogeneity spectrum of the mantle lid are known.
the distance and frequency dependence for Pn and Sn geometric spreading is sensitive to 2D random velocity heterogeneities in both the mantle lid and the Moho topography.
Pn geometric spreading is not expected to be frequency independent, and that the distance and frequency dependence is sensitive to the presence of heterogeneity in the mantle lid.
